primary_number: 59.11% informal (August 2023, BPS official headline from Sakernas); ISEAS/Fulcrum figure of 51.5% uses authors' own calculation from Sakernas microdata with a different ('simplified') definition
publisher: BPS (Badan Pusat Statistik / Statistics Indonesia) — Berita Resmi Statistik Ketenagakerjaan, November 2023 release covering August 2023 Sakernas
methodology_note: BPS uses three definitions of informality in Sakernas: (1) 'simplified' — job-based: covers casual workers without formal contracts, part-time, and unpaid household workers; (2) 'old' definition; (3) 'new' definition (see World Bank 2022 'Informality in Indonesia' policy paper, Annex 2). The headline BPS figure of 59.11% informal / 40.89% formal for August 2023 uses the employment-status classification: formal = employees/labourers + employers with permanent workers; informal = own-account workers, employers with unpaid/casual workers, casual agricultural workers, casual non-agricultural workers, and unpaid family workers. The ISEAS/Fulcrum 51.5% figure (cited in 'Growing or Shrinking? How Indonesia's Middle Class is Really Doing', fulcrum.sg) is described as 'SAKERNAS, authors' calculation' — i.e., a non-standard researcher derivation from Sakernas microdata, not the BPS official published figure. The two figures are not directly comparable. The BPS 59.11% is the authoritative primary-source figure.
urban_rural_split: Not directly confirmed from fetched pages (BPS bps.go.id pages were Cloudflare-blocked 403). Search snippets from ILOSTAT/Statista indicate rural informality in Indonesia is approximately 72.6% (2023) vs. lower urban rate — consistent with the national 59.11% being pulled down by lower urban informality. Urban informality is estimated at approximately 45-48% based on contextual evidence (the ~59% national figure with ~73% rural implies urban is approximately 45-48%). Exact BPS urban/rural breakdown unavailable from sources fetched due to access blocks.

recommended_edit_to_canonical: Replace the claim '51.5%' with the BPS official Sakernas August 2023 figure of 59.11% informal employment, and add a methodology note. Suggested revision: 'Indonesia's informal employment rate stood at 59.11% of the workforce (August 2023; BPS Sakernas, Berita Resmi Statistik November 2023), with rural informality estimated at ~72.6% vs. lower urban rates (~45-48%). The ISEAS/Fulcrum figure of 51.5% cited in some analyses reflects a non-standard authors' calculation from Sakernas microdata using BPS's

definition (covering casual/part-time/unpaid workers), not the BPS headline employment-status classification. Both figures confirm a structural majority of the Indonesian workforce lacks formal-sector employer benefits. Primary source: BPS bps.go.id (Cloudflare-blocked; recommend attended fetch of https://www.bps.go.id/en/pressrelease/2023/11/06/2002/ for direct primary citation).' The pain-point logic ('self-employed segment fully OOP') is confirmed and strengthened by either figure — the actual share is higher than 51.5%, not lower.
